main_text.head: SECT. VI.
main_text.p: Quod tamen non est ita absolutè in-telligendum, quin ut duplicem admittat exceptionem : quorum altera perfonam respicit jurantis , altera consensum supe-rioris. Quod ad jurantem attinet, sci-endum est vix quenquam qui gaudet usu rationis, ita plene sub alterius esse pote-state, quin ut sit quantum ad aliqua sal-tem sui juris. Et de his ita licet unicui-que statuere pro suo arbitrio, etiam in-consulto superiore, ut possit aliquo actu suo sine ejus licentia inducere sibi obli-gationem. Non debet Caii servus Titio operam suam locare, aut herilium bono-rum partem aliquam ei donare vel com-modare, sine consensu ipsius Caii: quia[?] in his quae ad obsequium praestandum, ac disponendum de bonis, vel ad quam-cunque familiae administrationem spe-ctant , habet pater-familias merum im-perium. Potest tamen Caii servus de {a}peculio suo , vel Caii filius de peculii Servus quod juravit servetur, si peculii administratione habuit. page.notes: Marginal note mark: the margin shows an asterisk, while the text shows a superscript "a" before "peculio". I took the mark to be "a" and put the same letter on both. Doubtful: "quia[?]", where the scan shows a ligature-like form after "qui". Catchword "nentur" is read from the lower right and completes "te-" at the line end. Long s is transcribed as s throughout. The running head is printed in italics in part; it is given here as plain text. The page ends mid-word ("te-"), which continues on the next page.
